candidates.source_name: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore (DRI) — official site
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's Supreme Audit Institution. Its audits of ministries, funds and state agencies routinely reconstruct procurement plans vs. execution, name suppliers and quantify direct awards (direktni sporazum) that never appear cleanly in CEJN. Primary oversight source for the cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of /revizorski-izvjestaji and /aktuelnost; harvest PDF links under /doc/*.pdf; PDF text extraction + supplier/amount NER. Note TLS chain issue observed — use a client with relaxed/complete CA bundle.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query (sr) + snowball from search result set
queries_used: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore izvještaj revizije javne nabavke
Montenegro state audit institution report public procurement IT contracts
candidates.observed_blocker: WebFetch on https://www.dri.co.me/revizorski-izvjestaji and https://dri.co.me/revizorski-izvjestaji returned 'unable to verify the first certificate'. Site is clearly live (indexed pages, live PDFs). Treated as unverified/bot-or-TLS issue, NOT dead.

candidates.source_name: DRI — Revizorski izvještaji archive (audit report repository, 2004–present)
candidates.why_relevant: The actual archive of final audit reports, filterable by year, audit type and audited entity. This is where regularity audits containing procurement findings live, going back roughly two decades — multi-year series no primary portal offers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate by year filter; store PDF + metadata (auditee, year, audit type); diff on new publications.
queries_used: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore izvještaj revizije javne nabavke
candidates.observed_blocker: Same TLS chain failure as parent domain on WebFetch; PDFs under /doc/ appear in search index.

candidates.source_name: DRI — IT / information-system audits (revizija informacionih sistema)
candidates.why_relevant: DRI runs a dedicated IT-audit line (2 IT audits in a recent year alongside 25 regularity and 6 performance audits). These reports describe the procured systems, the vendors, IT security/continuity gaps and the contracting history — the closest thing in Montenegro to an independent assessment of state IT/payment-adjacent system procurement.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword filter the report archive on 'informacion*' / 'IT revizija'; extract vendor names and system names for supplier mapping.
candidates.discovered_via_method: targeted sr query on IT-audit terminology, snowballed from DRI site structure
queries_used: DRI "revizija uspjeha" informacioni sistem Crna Gora izvještaj IT revizija dri.co.me

candidates.source_name: DRI — Godišnji izvještaj o izvršenim revizijama i aktivnostima (annual audit activity report)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual consolidated report giving the year's audit programme, systemic procurement findings and recommendation follow-up. Best single document for tracking which entities are under audit scrutiny and which procurement failure modes recur.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual pull; parse the recommendations tables.
queries_used: Državna revizorska institucija Crne Gore izvještaj revizije javne nabavke

candidates.source_name: Institut alternativa (IA) — public procurement research programme
candidates.why_relevant: The most methodical Montenegrin think-tank on procurement. Publishes recurring quantitative analyses of direct agreements (direktni sporazum), urgent/shortened procedures, simple purchases (jednostavne nabavke) and defence/security-sector procurement — with per-institution shares of spending. Exactly the reconstruction of contracts missing from the portal that this cell needs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /aktuelno (paginated news) and the publications section; monitor for 'nabavk*' keyword; download attached PDF analyses.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query (sr) + snowball across IA article set
queries_used: Institut alternativa monitoring javnih nabavki Crna Gora izvještaj
Institut alternativa "javne nabavke" publikacija analiza direktni sporazum Crna Gora 2025

candidates.why_relevant: Deep-paginated archive (140+ pages observed) that surfaces IA's own analyses plus references to other actors, official reports and datasets. A good snowball spine for discovering procurement-monitoring publications and events over a decade.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Paginated crawl with keyword filter; use as seed-expansion for actor names.
queries_used: Institut alternativa monitoring javnih nabavki Crna Gora izvještaj

candidates.why_relevant: IA-built structured database of Montenegrin budget execution from 2011 onward, searchable by economic and organizational classification. Lets you size the spending envelope (e.g. IT/services lines) of a bank-adjacent public buyer even when the individual contract is unpublished — a derived-data source no primary portal offers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Inspect for an underlying JSON/API endpoint behind the search UI; otherwise scripted query-and-scrape by institution and year.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sr query on IA data tools; URL inferred from portal name reported in coverage — treat exact URL as unverified

candidates.why_relevant: Municipal budget data for all Montenegrin local governments, maintained by IA for years. Municipalities are significant buyers of POS/IT/payment services and their direct-award share (~17% per IA) is where portal coverage is weakest.

negative_findings.description: Both https://www.dri.co.me/revizorski-izvjestaji and https://dri.co.me/revizorski-izvjestaji failed with 'unable to verify the first certificate' on WebFetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not enumerate the DRI audit-report archive structure directly. Search-engine evidence shows many live PDFs under dri.co.me/doc/ and live /aktuelnost/ pages, so the site is almost certainly up — this is a TLS-chain/fetch-client issue, NOT a dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: DRI is the single most important source in this cell; the collection pipeline must be configured with a full CA bundle (or an intermediate-fetching client) or it will silently drop the highest-value source.

negative_findings.description: MANS 'Javne nabavke' category index (https://www.mans.co.me/kategorija/javne-nabavke/) fetched successfully but rendered essentially one 2009 explainer article with no listed sub-items, reports or datasets.
negative_findings.result_summary: No downloadable MANS procurement dataset or report list was found at the obvious category URL in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: MANS's procurement material is likely behind tag pages, site search, or a separate publications/database section; a naive category crawl would wrongly conclude MANS publishes almost nothing on procurement.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated auditor/watchdog source was found that specifically covers procurement of BANKING or PAYMENT-sector IT (core banking, card/POS, payment infrastructure) in Montenegro.
negative_findings.result_summary: DRI IT audits located in this pass cover health (IZIS, health insurance fund, PCR app), sport registry and cultural-heritage systems. Watchdog procurement work (IA, MANS) is sector-agnostic or defence/security-focused.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For the banking/payments run scope, oversight coverage must be reached indirectly — via auditees that are financial in nature (Uprava prihoda i carina, Fond zdravstvenog osiguranja, Ministarstvo finansija, Centralna banka) rather than by topic search.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was exhausted before I could run planned queries on the parliamentary oversight track (Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet consideration of DRI reports) and on the procurement inspectorate's published findings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two intended snowball branches were not executed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The parliamentary committee track is where DRI findings become political follow-up and where non-published contracts sometimes get named; it remains an unexplored pointer branch for this cell.

negative_findings.description: mojnovac.me and mojgrad.me URLs were inferred from portal names reported in Montenegrin media coverage rather than fetched directly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portals are well documented as existing and IA-operated, but the exact live URLs and whether they expose machine-readable endpoints was not established in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are the only structured NGO-built spending datasets identified in the cell; their machine-readability determines whether they are a data source or just a browsing tool.

coverage_gaps.description: Internal audit function (interna revizija) inside ministries, state funds and the central bank, and the Ministry of Finance's central harmonisation unit for internal audit, were not covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search sr terms 'interna revizija', 'Centralna jedinica za harmonizaciju', 'godišnji izvještaj o internoj reviziji u javnom sektoru' and locate the consolidated annual internal-audit report.

coverage_gaps.description: Parliamentary oversight of audit findings (Skupština Crne Gore, Odbor za ekonomiju, finansije i budžet; Odbor za antikorupciju) not explored — search budget ran out.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl skupstina.me committee pages for sessions considering DRI reports and anti-corruption hearings; capture transcripts and submitted materials.

coverage_gaps.description: No auditor/watchdog output located that names IT or payment-services suppliers to Montenegrin public banks/financial institutions, which is the commercial core of the run scope.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pivot to entity-driven collection: enumerate DRI audits of financially-relevant auditees (Ministarstvo finansija, Uprava prihoda i carina, Fond PIO, Fond zdravstvenog osiguranja, Investiciono-razvojni fond, Centralna banka) and grep those PDFs for vendor names and 'informacioni sistem' procurement line items.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin-Cyrillic and alternative orthography variants (e.g. 'јавне набавке', 'ревизија') were not used as search variants; only Latin-script Montenegrin/Serbian and English were searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries in Cyrillic transliteration and with 'ijekavica' variants ('izvještaj' vs 'izveštaj', 'sprječavanje' vs 'sprečavanje' — note ASK itself appears under both spellings).

coverage_gaps.description: No check was made for RSS feeds, sitemaps, or open-data/API endpoints on dri.co.me, institut-alternativa.org, antikorupcija.me, so collection method recommendations are crawl-based assumptions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe /feed, /rss, /sitemap.xml and wp-json endpoints on the WordPress-based NGO sites (IA, MANS, CGO, CIN-CG all appear WordPress-based) to switch from scraping to structured feeds.

coverage_gaps.description: Transparency International's regional/national presence, the EU Commission's annual Montenegro country report (Chapter 5 – public procurement), and the EU Delegation's monitoring were not separately profiled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the EC enlargement country report series and TI regional procurement indices as external-oversight sources; they carry heavy weight in Montenegrin policy debate.

brief: Montenegro's audit-and-watchdog layer for procurement is small, well-defined and unusually productive: the State Audit Institution (DRI) anchors it with a two-decade archive of regularity, performance and — importantly for this run — dedicated information-system audits that name systems, vendors and IT-governance failures, while the Agency for Prevention of Corruption (ASK) adds annual/quarterly integrity and conflict-of-interest reporting. On the civil-society side, Institut alternativa supplies the quantitative work (shares of spending via direct agreements, urgent and shortened procedures, simple purchases, per-institution breakdowns) plus two NGO-built spending databases (mojnovac.me, mojgrad.me), MANS supplies FOI-extracted contracts that surface in the gov.me and parliamentary 'approved access' archives, and CGO, CIN-CG and the regional Balkan Tender Watch coalition fill in municipal, investigative and cross-country benchmarking angles; SIGMA/OECD and the OGP IRM provide external, methodologically consistent assessment. The key practical caveats: DRI's site failed TLS verification on every fetch attempt in this pass (almost certainly a certificate-chain issue on our side, not a dead source — do not mark it dead), MANS's procurement category index renders far thinner than the organisation's real output, and no watchdog product was found that targets banking or payment-sector IT procurement specifically. For the banking/payments scope this cell should therefore be worked entity-first — pulling DRI audits of financially-relevant auditees and grepping them for 'informacioni sistem' line items and supplier names — rather than topic-first.
